messages:
Maya (Sales): Heads-up — POC readout for Summit Energy finished. Sharing high-level numbers and proposed next steps. TL;DR: met latency SLO, 2 feature gaps, want pricing for dedicated plan.

Aadi (SE): Nice. Quick numbers pls (p50/p95 latency, tokens, queries/sec, cost delta vs baseline).

Liam (Customer Eng): From my run: p50=85ms, p95=220ms (tokenized avg prompt len ~380 tokens), peak QPS 42, sustained 20 QPS during sim. Token usage ~1.1M tokens/day on test workload.

Sophie (Product): Thanks Liam — can you also state eval pass/fail by success criteria? We defined: 1) <250ms p95, 2) 85% top-1 accuracy on golden prompts, 3) <3% hallucination rate on safety eval.

Liam (Customer Eng): Eval summary: accuracy = 82% (fell short), hallucination = 2.1% (passed), latency = passed. Detailed notes: accuracy regression tied to entity normalization for grid IDs — model often returns shortened forms that downstream matcher rejects.

Maya (Sales): Summit leadership asked: what would it take to hit accuracy target? also want a commercial proposal for Dedicated with burst to handle month-end spikes.

Aadi (SE): Technical path options: 1) prompt engineering + post-processing (quick, low cost) — expected +2–4% accuracy; 2) fine-tune or instruction-tuning with 5k in-domain examples (6–8 weeks) — +6–10%; 3) reranker ensemble: cheap rerank model + prompts (2–3 weeks) — +4–7%. Tradeoffs noted in doc.

Liam (Customer Eng): Quick mitigation we shipped during POC: added a post-filter that canonicalizes grid IDs via regex + fuzzy-match; that improved acceptance in the readout dataset by ~3.5%. I can package as a drop-in step for Summit.

Sophie (Product): For the readout deck we should show: baseline vs POC numbers, gap analysis, recommended path (short + long term), and acceptance runbook (who signs off on what). Also include quality regression test set and alert thresholds.

Maya (Sales): Pricing ask from Summit: estimate for Dedicated (8xA10G + 2xburst nodes) with 99.9 SLA and enterprise support. Can we get a ballpark?

Aadi (SE): Ballpark: reserved monthly commit for that shape ~ $48k/mo list, with burst pool add-on ~ $6k/mo retained. Discounts/term TBD. I'll run detailed cost model with usage profile from Liam and bake into proposal.

Liam (Customer Eng): One more technical note: KV cache hit rate was only 18% because customers vary prompts a lot. Recommend enabling prefix caching for recurring templates — should cut tokens by ~12%. I'll prepare a config snippet.

deploy-bot: deployment:canary finished — new post-filter rule v1.2 applied to summit-poc namespace at 2026-03-18T15:02:12Z :white_check_mark:

Maya (Sales): Great. For the readout next steps I suggest:
- Action 1: Liam to produce 'readout appendix' with dataset examples (due EOD tomorrow) — owner: Liam
- Action 2: Aadi to produce cost model + Dedicated proposal draft (due in 3 business days) — owner: Aadi
- Action 3: Sophie to prepare product recommendation slide + acceptance runbook (due in 2 business days) — owner: Sophie
- Action 4: Maya to assemble executive summary & commercial ask (pricing + next phase) and schedule follow-up with Summit (due in 4 business days) — owner: Maya

Aadi (SE): noted. I'll include two pricing scenarios: conservative (only reserved) and aggressive (reserved + burst with adaptive routing). Also will list assumptions: sustained QPS, peak window, token counts.

Liam (Customer Eng): I'll attach the eval id list and a short script to reproduce the acceptance run locally. Example command:

```
python tools/run_eval.py --dataset summit_readout.jsonl --model redwood-4o --batch 32 --prefix-cache on
```

Maya (Sales): One risk to flag for Summit: if they want to move to on-prem/private, timeline to full Private deploy is ~8–12 weeks with security questionnaire and infra prep. Call that out.

Sophie (Product): Agreed. Also call out monitoring guardrails: token-level budget alerts, per-route latency SLOs, and automatic fallback to smaller model during congestion.

Maya (Sales): Perfect. I'll assemble the readout deck this afternoon and share a draft link here when done. Any other blockers?

Aadi (SE): none from infra side. Need Summit to approve collection of 5k labeled examples if we pursue tuning.

Liam (Customer Eng): No blockers. I'll send the appendix by EOD.

Sophie (Product): No blockers — will post slides by Tuesday morning.

Maya (Sales): Thanks team :pray: — will post draft here: <https://redwood.internal/summit-poc/readout-draft> and set follow-up meeting for next Thu.
